title: Ishinomaki — 石巻
goal: Describe a place and distinguish a place category from its name.

cards.title: Looking at a Place through Pictures

blocks.text: Ishinomaki is a coastal city associated with Ishinomori Manga Museum. Our practice scene uses two fictional photographs and a book. You do not need the museum's difficult name spelling to learn today's Japanese.
**石巻で写真を見ました。** いしのまきで しゃしんを みました。 — I looked at photographs in Ishinomaki.

Rather than repeat the first lesson on kanji, use the skills you already have: recognise a familiar component, learn the whole location reading, and connect a new description to a noun. Keep cultural context separate from the details of our imaginary pictures.

items: **Character:** 石 · **Useful meaning/reading:** stone; いし, セキ/シャク · **Radical and visible parts:** 石, いし; upper strokes and lower 口-like section · **Role:** Formal review from Morioka.

**Character:** 巻 · **Useful meaning/reading:** roll/wind; まく/まき, カン · **Radical and visible parts:** Historical 卩/㔾 indexing family; some dictionaries use 己 for modern 巻. Upper 龹-like section and lower curl · **Role:** Encounter review from 花巻.

blocks.text: **石巻 / いしのまき** includes a spoken **の** that is not a separate written の in the name. Do not insert the noun-connecting particle into the spelling. Hanamaki and Ishinomaki share 巻, but their complete readings and locations differ. Indexing variation does not affect the required whole-name reading.

cards.title: 町: The Word We Have Used Already

blocks.text: **町 / まち — town; neighbourhood.** Radical **田**, た, with **丁** on the right. 丁 belongs to the character's historical sound structure. The field-like left is a recognition clue, not proof that every modern town is farmland.
**この町はきれいです。** この まちは きれいです。 — This town is beautiful.

まち can describe an urban area in ordinary speech without making a legal claim about municipal status. Today's formal attention is to the spelling. **町の店 / まちのみせ**, a shop in the town, reuses の. Do not treat every earlier use of 町 as having already taught all its readings.

**市 / し — city in names and administrative labels; 仙台市 / せんだいし — Sendai City; 石巻市 / いしのまきし — Ishinomaki City.** 市 is indexed under **巾**, はば; notice the lower cloth-shaped component beneath the upper strokes. Its historical market/city connection is orientation, not a required etymology exercise.
**石巻市は宮城にあります。** いしのまきしは みやぎに あります。 — Ishinomaki City is in Miyagi.
In the proper name 石巻市, the suffix 市 is し. Do not read it as まち just because both concern places. A word and its context determine the reading.

**村 / むら — village.** Radical **木**, きへん, with **寸** on the right. 寸 is associated with historical sound structure. A modern village is not defined by “tree + measure”; that would be an invented meaning formula.
**あの村に川があります。** あの むらに かわが あります。 — There is a river in that village.

This is a fictional village in a practice picture, not another location chapter. Compare 町 / まち, 市 / し in city names, and 村 / むら. Learn the useful word in its setting. The whole Journey will later add additional place-name suffixes and administrative vocabulary.

**新しい / あたらしい — new; 新しい本 / あたらしいほん — a new book.** 新 has indexing radical **斤**, おのづくり, on the right. The modern left contains 立-like and 木-like sections. These help you recognise a complex character; do not add their everyday meanings and claim that the sum explains “new.”
**これは新しい本です。** これは あたらしい ほんです。 — This is a new book.
新しい has several kana after 新. Okurigana preserve the whole adjective's reading and inflection. Notice that the kanji supplies **あたら** in this word, not a fixed one-syllable sound.
**古い / ふるい — old; 古い写真 / ふるいしゃしん — an old photograph.** 古 is indexed under **口**, くち; the modern shape has 十 above 口. That is a useful recognition pattern, not a calculation “ten mouths = old.”
**これは古い写真です。** これは ふるい しゃしんです。 — This is an old photograph.

For now use 古い for things such as pictures, books and buildings. It is not our word for an elderly person. **新しい本** and **古い本** make an opposite pair. “Old photograph” refers to its age; it does not necessarily mean the photographed object is old.
**この本は新しいです。その本は古いです。** この ほんは あたらしいです。その ほんは ふるいです。 — This book is new. That book is old.
Both use an い-adjective at the end of the sentence. **この本は新しくないです。** この ほんは あたらしくないです。 — This book is not new.

The negative replaces final い with くない, following the adjective pattern you already met. 新しくない does not mean 古い in every possible context: a book can be neither recently new nor very old. Grammar negates a description; it does not automatically substitute its opposite.

cards.title: A Name, a Category, a Description

blocks.text: **石巻は宮城の市です。** いしのまきは みやぎの しです。 — Ishinomaki is a city in Miyagi.
**この写真は町の写真です。** この しゃしんは まちの しゃしんです。 — This photograph is a photograph of a town.
**その写真は村の写真です。** その しゃしんは むらの しゃしんです。 — That photograph is a photograph of a village.

The first identifies a real location's category; the next two describe fictional images. の connects nouns. A description need not contain every new kanji: sentences are useful because they are natural and understandable, not because they maximise the number of new characters per line.

cards.title: Put the Description in a Past Account

blocks.text: **石巻で新しい本を買いました。** いしのまきで あたらしい ほんを かいました。 — I bought a new book in Ishinomaki.
**店で古い写真を見ました。** みせで ふるい しゃしんを みました。 — I looked at old photographs at a shop.

Past tense is on the action verb 買いました/見ました. The adjective before the noun stays 新しい/古い. This differs from saying “The book was new,” where the description itself is past; we will practise that distinction in Shiroishi. Read the ending that carries the time information.

items: Read 石巻市. **Answer:** いしのまきし.
Which word means village: 村 / 市 / 新? **Answer:** 村 / むら.
Which component links 村 to 松? **Answer:** 木.
Translate 新しい本. **Answer:** a new book.
Make 新しいです negative in the taught polite style. **Answer:** 新しくないです.
Does 古い写真 require that the photographed building itself is old? **Answer:** No; it describes the photograph unless context supplies more information.

blocks.text: 石巻 is いしのまき; the spoken の is part of the name. 石 is review; 巻 remains an assisted encounter. 町 is まち; 市 is し in our city labels; 村 is むら. 新しい and 古い describe things. い-adjectives retain their ending before a noun and use くない for the taught negative.
**Recall task:** “I bought a new book in Ishinomaki.” **Model:** 石巻で新しい本を買いました。 Continue to Shiroishi and add distance and price descriptions.
